pantry_staples_assumed: an array of typical dried seasonings (garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cumin, oregano, chili flakes, bay leaves, etc.)
preferences.pantry_staples_note: never add these to the shopping list. Only add a spice/pantry item when a recipe needs something genuinely uncommon she likely doesn't have (e.g. ras el hanout, a specific chile).
preferences.restock_logic: each week, infer likely-depleted items from the PRIOR week's dinners (e.g. a fully-used spice jar, the last of a produce item, low pantry basics implied by what was cooked) and add those - don't just repeat a fixed list. Always add eggs (1 dozen) every week regardless, since her supply runs low - standing item until she says otherwise.

preferences.teach_each_week: one new cuisine + one new cooking technique
preferences.artifact_color_scheme: pink and black - deep magenta/hot pink accent against near-black in dark mode, and against a soft pink-white ground in light mode. Keep this scheme for future weeks unless she asks to change it.
preferences.recipe_sourcing: each dinner must be adapted from a specific, well-reviewed published recipe (NYT Cooking, Bon Appetit, Serious Eats, America's Test Kitchen, Once Upon a Chef, etc.) with the source cited and adaptations listed - never written with no source
preferences.pricing: web-search current prices for stores near the zip above where possible; flag anything unverified as an estimate
preferences.circulars: each week, also web-search the current weekly circular/sale flyer for each store in 'stores' (ShopRite, Trader Joe's, Whole Foods, Food Bazaar) and route items to whichever store has them on sale that week where it makes sense; note in the plan when a specific circular deal was found and used, and note when no matching deal turned up rather than skipping the check silently
preferences.landing_artifact_note: she added this URL to her phone home screen as a permanent app icon. Every week's plan MUST publish to this exact URL via the Artifact tool's `url` param (not a fresh artifact) so the same home-screen icon always shows the current week. Still also save a dated copy under meal-prep/weeks/ in the repo for history.
preferences.advance_prep_highlighting: any recipe step that must be done a specific number of hours (or longer) ahead of cooking (dry-brining, marinating, soaking, overnight-anything) must get a visually distinct highlighted callout at the top of that recipe card (not buried in the numbered steps), stating exactly when to start it relative to that dinner's day of the week.
preferences.advance_prep_reminders: whenever a week's plan includes an advance-prep step, schedule an actual push-notification reminder (via create_trigger, run_once_at, create_new_session_on_fire=true, notifications:{push:true}) timed to land at the moment she needs to start that step (e.g. the morning/evening before, per the recipe's lead time) for that specific date. The reminder message should name the dish and the exact action to take.
preferences.pre_shopping_check: every week's artifact must include a 'Pre-shopping check' section, placed before the store shopping lists, as an interactive checklist grouped into Pantry / Fridge / Freezer cards (same tap-to-flag pattern as the shopping list, but tapping marks an item 'missing - add to list' rather than checked-off, since the point is catching gaps before leaving, not marking done). List every staple/seasoning that week's recipes assume she has (salt, pepper, oil, the specific dried spices each recipe calls for, anything less-common like fennel seed) plus a fridge/freezer prompt to use up leftovers before buying more. Explicitly call out anything that's new this week and therefore NOT assumed (e.g. a spice blend she's never bought before) so it doesn't get missed on the actual shopping list.

weekly_schedule.mon_thu: work 8:00-9:15am, FREE 9:15am-2:40pm, work 2:40-6:00pm, zoom class away from home 6:00-9:00pm, home/free from ~9:00pm on
weekly_schedule.fri_sun: busy/unpredictable - do not assume free time, don't schedule cooking sessions here

preferences.cooking_schedule_logic: she cannot cook fresh on weeknights - she isn't home until ~9pm on Mon-Thu, too late to cook and eat properly. All cooking happens in TWO batch sessions during the Mon-Thu 9:15am-2:40pm free window (never at night, never on weekends): Session 1 on MONDAY midday covers the first two dinners of the week (start the longest/most-unattended braise or stew first, do the second dish while it simmers); Session 2 on WEDNESDAY midday covers the remaining two dinners. Every weeknight dinner (eaten ~9pm+) is a reheat only, never fresh cooking. When a dish needs advance prep (dry-brining, marinating), time it to land the evening before its batch-cook session (e.g. if Session 2 is Wednesday midday, brine Tuesday ~9pm when she gets home from class) so the push reminder fires then, not at some other arbitrary time. Build each week's 4 dinners with this 2-session structure in mind: prefer 1 longer/mostly-unattended dish (braise/stew) + 1 quicker dish per session, mirroring what has worked (barbacoa + rigatoni in session 1, tagine + blackened chicken in session 2).
